findings.problem: The two proofs repeat the same argument. Both prove positivity of the completions count and of the remaining count. Both state a factorisation `|completions| = |remaining| * m` through `card_completions_eq`. Both unfold the uniform PMF measure, convert to real division, and clear denominators with `div_eq_div_iff`. They differ only in the event, and in whether `nlinarith` or `rw [hfactor, hevent]; ring` closes the goal. In fact `next_value_probability` is the special case `P := (· = a)` of the general statement.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one helper after `card_completions_eq`:
`theorem uniform_toReal_of_card_mul (K) (base) (p : (I ↪ J) → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (n r m : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) (hC : (completions K base).card = r * m) (hp : ((completions K base).filter p).card = n * m) : ((PMF.uniformOfFinset (completions K base) (completions_nonempty K base)).toOuterMeasure {e | p e}).toReal = (n : ℝ) / r`.
Proof sketch:
1. `m ≠ 0` follows from `Finset.card_pos` applied to `completions_nonempty`, together with `hC`.
2. `rw [PMF.toOuterMeasure_uniformOfFinset_apply]`, then `simp only [ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_natCast, Set.mem_ofPred_eq]`.
3. `rw [hC, hp]; push_cast; field_simp`.

Then `next_event_probability` becomes `uniform_toReal_of_card_mul K base (fun e => P (e i)) _ _ _ (card_pos of ⟨base i, base_mem_remaining ..⟩) (card_completions_eq K base i hi (base i) _) (event_card_eq K base i hi P)`.

`next_value_probability` becomes the same call with `n := 1`, `p := fun e => e i = a`, `hC := card_completions_eq K base i hi a ha`, and `hp := (one_mul _).symm`. Here `(1:ℕ):ℝ` needs a `Nat.cast_one` rewrite. Alternatively, derive it from `next_event_probability` with `P := (· = a)` and `Finset.card_eq_one`. This works because `(remaining K base).filter (· = a) = {a}` when `ha` holds.
findings.benefit: Each probability theorem shrinks to a short instantiation. The measure-to-cardinality conversion and denominator clearing live in one place. A change to the PMF API, such as a rename of `toOuterMeasure_uniformOfFinset_apply`, is then fixed once. The two theorems no longer differ only through duplicated `hC`/`hR`/`hfactor` boilerplate and an ad hoc `nlinarith`.

findings.excerpt:
Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (fun e he =>
        value_mem_remaining K base e he i hi)
findings.problem: Both lemmas use the same argument. Split the relevant set into fibres over `remaining K base` with `Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise` and `value_mem_remaining`. Then use `fibre_card_eq` to make every fibre have the size of one reference fibre. Finally collapse the constant sum with `simp`. `card_completions_eq` is the case `P := fun _ => True` of `event_card_eq`. `event_card_eq` redoes the fibre decomposition and adds a `hfibre` ext-proof to strip the predicate. It is also fixed to the reference value `base i`, so `card_completions_eq` cannot be derived from it as stated.
findings.proposed_change:
Generalise `event_card_eq` to take an arbitrary `a ∈ remaining K base` in place of `base i`. Its conclusion becomes `((completions K base).filter (fun e => P (e i))).card = ((remaining K base).filter P).card * ((completions K base).filter (fun e => e i = a)).card`. The existing proof goes through with `fibre_card_eq K base i b a hb ha`.

Then prove `card_completions_eq` by `have := event_card_eq K base i hi (fun _ => True) a ha; simpa using this`. `simp` should reduce `filter (fun _ => True)` to the whole finset via `Finset.filter_true`.

`next_event_probability` would then instantiate `a := base i` with `base_mem_remaining`.
findings.benefit: One fibre-decomposition proof replaces two near-identical `calc` blocks. `card_completions_eq` is no longer a second copy of the argument, and the fibre-count lemma is stated once at full generality.
